Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with ~1 week of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic discomfort, and pink urine; no fever, flank/back pain, or GI red flags; clinical impression is uncomplicated cystitis; urine testing arranged and empiric antibiotics discussed; safety-net advice given.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination (burning/stinging), increased urinary frequency, and lower abdominal (suprapubic) aching pain worse with urination; noticed pink-tinged urine today.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms initially described as “a few days/3 days,” later clarified to “just under a week” (conflict noted; patient clarified ~1 week).
  - First episode; patient states this has not happened before.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies fever/temperature.
  - Denies nausea/vomiting.
  - Denies back or flank pain; pain does not radiate.
  - Denies abnormal vaginal discharge.
- GU/gynecologic:
  - Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; typically does not use condoms.
  - On combined oral contraceptive pill.
  - Last menstrual period: ~2 weeks ago.
  - Unprotected intercourse (no condom): ~1–2 weeks ago.
- GI:
  - Baseline IBS with variable bowel habits (alternating consistency and frequency); no new bowel symptoms.
- General: Eating and drinking adequately.
- Systems review: Pertinent negatives as above.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) — variable stool consistency and frequency; uses antispasmodic for cramps. No new GI symptoms.
- No other medical conditions reported.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- IBS medication (antispasmodic “begins with M”; specific name not captured) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Clindamycin — reaction not described.

Social History:
- University student (studying English); recently started course.
- Lives in university halls with a flatmate; family lives outside London and is supportive.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially.
- Substances: Tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago; counseled to avoid ongoing use.

Family History:
- No known family history of bladder or kidney problems. No other relevant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented (no examination performed; no vitals recorded).

Investigations:
- Plan for urine sample drop-off at practice for urinalysis and laboratory culture/sensitivity; results pending.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis (UTI) with hematuria
  - Assessment: Dysuria, frequency, suprapubic aching, pink-tinged urine; no fever, flank pain, or vomiting. First episode.
  - Plan:
    - Start empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin (3-day course); specific agent not documented.
    - Encourage oral hydration.
    - Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.
    - Submit urine sample for urinalysis and culture; clinic to contact with results and adjust antibiotics if needed.
    - Safety net: Seek care urgently for fever, back/flank pain, or vomiting; return if no improvement by next week.
- Issue 2: Contraception and pregnancy consideration
  - Assessment: On combined pill; recent unprotected intercourse; LMP 2 weeks ago. No pregnancy testing performed at this visit.
  - Plan: No specific actions documented; pregnancy to be kept in mind if symptoms persist (per clinician comment).
- Issue 3: IBS — stable
  - Assessment: Baseline variable bowel habits; no change from usual.
  - Plan: Continue current IBS medication (name not captured).

General Plan items:
- Urine drop-off arranged at practice; point-of-care testing and send-out to lab; follow-up with results.
- Advised to avoid cannabis use going forward.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements:
  - No vitals or physical exam documented.
  - Exact IBS medication name and dosing not captured.
  - Specific antibiotic chosen not documented.
  - Allergy reaction details (type/severity) not described.
  - Past surgical history, immunization status, and comprehensive medication reconciliation not obtained.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Symptom duration reported as “3 days” vs “just under a week”; patient clarified to “just under a week” (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional indistinct/missing words (e.g., exact IBS medication name not captured).
